# Independent receiving review: exterior mixed-qubit decoder
2026-10-29. ACCEPTED under the exact stated encoding and ideal known-control interface.

Let H=L tensor J have dimension m=2r. Restricting P_wedge on B^tensor m to V^tensor m H^tensor m is the rank-one determinant projector. This is true for any ambient D>=m; choosing computational wedge outcomes may expose multiple proportional amplitudes but cannot introduce a logical-dependent output vector. For each fixed junk tuple, singlet contraction maps the incoming logical qubit to the retained m-1 reference qubits. The determinant of U tensor I_J is one for U in SU(2). Singlet invariance consequently yields M_alpha U=U^tensor(m-1) M_alpha. Complete reducibility and Schur's lemma yield M_alpha=I_L tensor v_alpha in the known spin-1/2 block, with no other-spin component. This proves CP identity on all operators, including arbitrary external reference extension; it is not merely a state-fidelity argument.

Linear combinations of these intertwiners remain intertwiners. Thus an arbitrary purification of jointly correlated junk, initially independent of all logical inputs and references, leaves an input-independent residual state after successful extraction. This is stronger than classical mixture robustness but does NOT authorize an interacting source memory whose one-call marginal happens to look like N. The same V on every call and the initial product between junk and all logical systems remain load-bearing.

For independent junk sigma, tau=(I_2/2) tensor sigma on the common support. The determinant multilinear identity gives success det(tau) Tr(tau^-1 N(rho))/m. The trace equals m, hence p=(det sigma)^2/2^(2r). This is input independent and ambient-D independent. Singular sigma has zero success by continuity (or lack of enough occupied support dimensions). The supplied r is the actual ambient junk dimension; overestimating its occupied rank destroys success, and underestimating a higher-rank encoder does not satisfy this theorem. There is no rank-learning procedure implicit here.

Bell-to-singlet conversion by known Y on retained references is consistent with the intertwiner orientation; overall phases are irrelevant. A known Schur transform with a calibrated conventional spin basis extracts the original qubit, not its transpose or conjugate. On unsupported sectors a total decoder can output any fixed stat
